punchline: At Chernobyl, the emergency button meant to stop the reactor made its power rise first.
thirty_sec: On the night of April 26, 1986, a safety test was running at Chernobyl's reactor four. Power fell to about 30 megawatts, and the operators pulled out the control rods to raise it. At 1:23 a.m. someone pressed the AZ-5 emergency shutdown button. But the rods had graphite tips, which first increased power as they entered the core, and the reactor exploded. The flaw had shown up before and nobody had told the operators. Adam Higginbotham's book shows why blaming only the operators falls short.
